title: etbb-july-2024-february-2026-update.pdf — section 434
text:
132. Conversely, it is important to be aware that people whose first language is Welsh may
nevertheless opt to speak in English, because they are less than confident about using
Welsh in a legal setting.

133. In some cases, Welsh speakers may be embarrassed by their lack of knowledge of technical
Welsh terms and therefore reluctant to use the language in contexts which may expose that
fact. This can affect professionals in technical fields as much as lay members of the public.
This sometimes arises with vocabulary in technical fields where English has traditionally
been the language of discourse.

134. There is no recognised body in Wales responsible for standardising terms, so it can also
happen that Welsh speakers use an English word because they are unsure of the “correct”
Welsh version. For example, there are at least three Welsh versions of the English term
“Youth Offending Team/Service”.
